note: Re-judged 2026-11-10 (independent auditor, not the author of the change) after responder_eap.go::handleResponderEAP changed in 31f16fc038. RFC 3748 Section 4: "Since EAP only defines Codes 1-4, EAP packets with other codes MUST be silently discarded by both authenticators and peers." The change adds, after the unchanged eapMessageDiscarded(err) arm, a call to discardUnauthenticatedHandshakeRequest that drops a round whose decryptAndParse error is not errInnerParse, and rewords the WARN for the authenticated-malformed arm that still sets StateDead. The RFC 3748 discard runs first, so an encrypted EAP packet with an undefined Code still returns through the same arm before the new branch is reached, and the new branch only widens what is dropped without state change (a round that fails its integrity check), so it cannot turn a silent discard into a state change. fsm.go::handleEAPResponse, responder.go::handleResponderInbound, eap.go::Process and peer.go::Process are unchanged since the 2026-11-08 judgement. The three tagged units are unchanged: TestEngineDiscardedEAPCodesPreserveExchange sends encrypted Codes 0, 5 and 255 into both IKE roles in StateEAPInProgress through handleInbound and asserts state, expected Message ID, last sent message and retransmission state unchanged, then a held-back valid packet at the same Message ID completes both roles with matching nonzero MSKs and a verified AUTH; the core units assert the authenticator answers nothing for Codes 0, 5, 255 and wrong-role Codes, and the peer reports a discard with no response, error, Done or MSK, with state, method and round budget unchanged, before legitimate MS-CHAPv2 packets complete the exchange. Those encrypted packets pass their integrity check, so they still reach the eapMessageDiscarded arm and the engine unit still discriminates it. Verdict stands. Tests not re-run by this judge.
